hero.title: Can you swap to a cheaper car?
hero.p1: Compare keeping your financed vehicle with replacement options. The headline number is all-in monthly cost — loan payment plus insurance, maintenance, and fuel or electricity — so a lower payment that burns more gas does not fool the math.
hero.p2: province-aware vehicle taxes (including BC PST-116 trade-in rules), EV rebates, multi-scenario trade-in ranges, field overrides, and a reverse max-budget solve for your target all-in payment.

methodology.title: How the math works
methodology.p1: Everything runs in your browser; inputs never leave your device. All-in monthly cost is the sum of a frequency-normalized auto loan payment plus insurance, maintenance & repairs, and fuel or electricity.
methodology.p2: Auto loans use monthly compounding (APR ÷ periods per year), not Canadian mortgage semi-annual compounding. Vehicle taxes follow provincial rules; BC applies PST-116 (rate from full price, tax on net after trade-in). Rules last reviewed for {{rulesDate}}.
methodology.taxBody: For dealer purchases in BC, the PST rate is looked up from the full purchase price, then applied to purchase price minus trade-in. GST is 5% on the same net. Federal luxury tax (if any) uses the pre-tax price and is not reduced by trade-in. Private sales do not get a trade-in tax credit.
methodology.maxBody: Operating costs are subtracted from your target all-in to get loan payment room. That payment is inverted to a max amount financed, then a binary search finds the highest pre-tax purchase price whose taxes, rebates, trade equity, and down payment produce that financed amount.
methodology.disclaimer: Not financial or tax advice. Estimates for educational sensitivity analysis. Confirm with your dealer, lender, and provincial registry.
